/-!
# Erdős Problem 871

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/871](https://www.erdosproblems.com/871)
- [ErNa88] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of bases*. J. Number Theory (1988), 1-9.
- [ErNa89] Erdős, Paul and Nathanson, Melvyn B., *Additive bases with many representations*. Acta Arith. (1989), 399-406.
-/

namespace Erdos871

/--
Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, and suppose $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Can $A$ be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases of order $2$?

A question of Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa88], who proved this is true if $1_A\ast 1_A(n) > c\log n$ (for all large $n$) for some constant $c>(\log\frac{4}{3})^{-1}$. Erdős and Nathanson [ErNa89] also proved that for every $t$ there exists a basis $A$ of order $2$ such that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\geq t$ for all large $n$ and yet $A$ cannot be partitioned into two disjoint additive bases. This has been disproved by Larsen using Claude Opus 4.5 - in fact only a small modification of the argument of [ErNa89] is required.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos871.lean"]
theorem erdos_871 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
        (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a + b = n) ∧
        (∀ t, ∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ pairs : Finset (ℕ × ℕ),
          pairs.card ≥ t ∧
            ∀ p ∈ pairs, p.1 ∈ A ∧ p.2 ∈ A ∧ p.1 + p.2 = n ∧ p.1 ≤ p.2) →
        ∃ (B C : Set ℕ),
          (∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ B ∨ x ∈ C) ∧
          Disjoint B C ∧
          (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ B, ∃ b ∈ B, a + b = n) ∧
          (∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop, ∃ a ∈ C, ∃ b ∈ C, a + b = n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos871

findings.description: The background citation in the docstring (line 33) mixes representation-count normalizations. It attributes to ErNa88 a sufficient condition on the ordered convolution 1_A∗1_A with c > (log(4/3))⁻¹. The paper gives that constant for the unordered count u_A(n), counting a ≤ b. Since 1_A∗1_A(n) = 2u_A(n) − δ_A(n), where δ_A(n) ∈ {0,1}, the equivalent logarithmic condition in ordered-convolution notation has c > 2(log(4/3))⁻¹. The source webpage repeats this normalization slip. This affects only the background reference: the formal theorem's divergence condition is faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Nathanson, Partitions of bases into disjoint unions of bases (1988), Theorem 3, pp. 5–6, and §3, Problem 2, p. 8, explicitly count representations with a_i ≤ a_j and give the threshold c > (log(4/3))⁻¹: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1988-25.pdf. The website defines convolution as f∗g(n) = ∑_{a+b=n} f(a)g(b), i.e. the ordered count: https://www.erdosproblems.com/definitions.
findings.suggested_fix: In the background logarithmic-bound sentence, either use an explicitly defined unordered representation count, or retain convolution and change the threshold to c > 2(log(4/3))⁻¹. No change to the Lean theorem is needed.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses divergence using finite witnesses of at least t unordered representations, with p.1 ≤ p.2, rather than a limit of the ordered convolution used on the source webpage.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed n, all representations are finite in number because both summands lie between 0 and n. Thus the finite-witness condition is equivalent to u_A(n) ≥ t, where u_A counts all unordered representations. If R_A is the ordered convolution, then u_A(n) ≤ R_A(n) ≤ 2u_A(n). Consequently, ∀ t, eventually u_A(n) ≥ t is equivalent to R_A(n) → ∞. This equivalence, including equality of the ordered count with the finite indicator convolution, was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Taking t = 1 also proves the separately stated basis hypothesis is redundant, not restrictive.
